archetype.name: Playoff Team (two-star offense)
archetype.definition: A team whose results run through an elite guard-center pairing in Murray and Jokić, good enough to win most nights. The thin wing group and a middling defense keep it closer to the playoff pack than to the West's elite.

report.headline: Murray and Jokić are carrying a team whose wings and defensive glass lag.
report.take:
Denver at 7-4 looks a lot like the Denver of recent years with the margins shaved. The Nuggets have won 48 to 57 games in each of the last five seasons and finished first in offensive rating last year. This version has a Net Rtg of 1.9 (13th), sits 15th on the site, and its record is close to honest. W vs Pt Diff is +1, and the margin alone implies six wins rather than seven. A six-point overtime win over New Orleans is the one result doing more work than it should. Otherwise this is a slightly-above-average team by the numbers, and the record says the same.

The engine is two players. Jamal Murray is the story of the first month: a 66.4 TS %, a 6.5 BPM, and an On-Off of +24.3, third on the point guard tab. Jokić is second on the center tab with an 8.5 BPM and 100 assists, which is why the backcourt grades an A and the frontcourt a B. The offense still protects the ball, with a TOV % of 12.1 that ranks 5th, and it gets to the line, with a FT Rate of 31.1 that ranks 7th. The problem is everything around those two. The wing group grades an F. DeMar DeRozan has the most wing minutes but a 49.8 TS %, a -5.2 BPM and an On-Off of -18, and Tyus Jones's minutes have gone badly at -24.7. Bench units are giving back what the stars build.

What the record hides is a stylistic drift. Denver takes only 36.4% of its shots from three, 28th in the league and well under the 43.3 league average, and it is hitting 34.9% after shooting 39.6% last year. ORtg has slid from 122.6 to 117.5, which is still 9th. On the other end, the 19th-ranked defense is consistent with the 21st-ranked units of the last two years, so that part is not new. The rebounding is new: a DRB % of 71.4 (22nd) against 75.3 last season. Opposing forwards are feasting, with power forwards scoring at a rate that ranks 29th and small forwards 28th. Centers, meanwhile, are held to the fewest points in the league.

The direction is encouraging. November has been a 4-2 month with 110.83 allowed a game against 115.2 in October, and the last five games went 4-1 at +6.8 a game. That run came mostly against soft opponents, though, and the one good team in it, Houston, beat them by ten. The coming week is the honest test.

strengths.title: Murray playing like a star
strengths.body: Murray's efficiency and impact are elite through 11 games: a 66.4 TS % at 26.4 USG %, with the team dramatically better when he plays. That shooting will cool somewhat, but he is the reason the backcourt grades an A. A version of him even a notch lower still keeps this offense top-10.

strengths.title: Jokić-run offense that doesn't waste trips
strengths.body: Even with three-point volume near the bottom of the league, Denver ranks 6th in TS % and 5th in TOV %. That is the Jokić signature of clean, high-value possessions and trips to the line. It is structural rather than luck and has held across every season in the history block.

strengths.title: Centers neutralized
strengths.body: Opposing centers score fewer points against Denver than against any other team, 4.04 below their own averages. Combined with point guards held well under their norms, the interior and point-of-attack matchups are holding. The leaks are elsewhere.

concerns.title: An F wing group
concerns.body: The small forward minutes are a hole at both ends. DeRozan is inefficient and deeply negative on the floor, and the young wings behind him haven't stabilized it. Opposing small forwards and power forwards are taking a share of points well above the league's against this team. Unless the rotation changes or Cameron Johnson absorbs more of these minutes, this is the most durable weakness on the roster.

concerns.title: Losing the defensive glass
concerns.body: A DRB % of 71.4 ranks 22nd, a real drop from 75.3 last season. Opponents also finish 66.6% at the rim (20th) on an above-average share of rim attempts. The middling defense is a multi-year trait, but giving away second chances is new. With the league's best offensive-rebounding teams on the schedule, it is the number to watch.

concerns.title: Three-point volume has dried up
concerns.body: Denver ranks 28th in 3PA Rate and is shooting 34.9% from deep after 39.6% last year, a big reason ORtg dipped from 122.6 to 117.5. Some of the percentage should come back. The low volume looks like a roster choice: the wings combine for very few made threes.

trend.note: October was a 3-2 month with a negative margin. November is 4-2 with the defense allowing far fewer points, and the last five games went 4-1 at +6.8 a game, though mostly against weaker opponents.

weekAhead.headline: Two soft games bracket a Boston-Houston gut check at home
weekAhead.body:
Three of four games are in Denver. The bookends should be wins: Phoenix ranks 26th in defense and last in DRB %, and Chicago ranks 28th in defense and allows the most rim attempts in the league. Both matchups favor Murray and Jokić. Phoenix gives up the second-most points to opposing centers, and Chicago lets point guards beat their own averages by nearly five.

The middle is the measuring stick. Boston (11-2, first on the site) has the league's best Net Rtg and second-best defense, and it protects the rim better than almost anyone. Houston (11-3, second on the site) already beat Denver 100-110 and brings the 2nd-ranked offense, the 2nd-best ORB %, and A+ wings and frontcourt. Those are exactly the areas where Denver is weakest. A 3-1 week would say the November surge is real. A 2-2 week would confirm the sheet's view of a solid but non-elite team.

keyMatchups.title: Houston's offensive glass vs Denver
keyMatchups.body: Houston rebounds 32.4% of its own misses, 2nd in the league, while Denver ranks 22nd in DRB %. That mismatch, plus Houston's A+ wings against Denver's F group, fed the earlier ten-point loss. Unless Denver finishes defensive possessions, the rematch tilts Houston's way even at home.

keyMatchups.title: Jokić against Boston's rim defense
keyMatchups.body: Boston holds opponents to 59.3% at the rim (2nd) and keeps centers well below their averages. Denver's low-volume three-point attack can't simply go around that. Boston also takes 49% of its shots from three at 38.5%, so Denver likely needs a big perimeter night to keep pace.

keyMatchups.title: Soft defenses for the stars
keyMatchups.body: Phoenix ranks 29th in points allowed to centers and 30th to point guards. Chicago is 28th in defensive rating. These are the nights for Murray and Jokić to pad the margin and for the bench to get minutes without paying for them.

weekAhead.watch: Denver's defensive rebounding against Houston: if the Rockets win the glass again, the November defensive improvement was mostly the schedule.

restOfSeason.body:
The sheet's pace of 52 wins assumes the 7-4 start holds, while the margin points a little lower. My range sits just under that pace. The offense is the most likely part to improve: a Jokić-Murray attack that led the league last year is unlikely to keep shooting 34.9% from three. The defense ranking near 20th looks like who this team has been for three seasons. A roughly league-average defense is real, and the rebounding slip should partly recover but may not return to last year's level with these forwards.

The ceiling depends on the wing minutes. As long as DeRozan and the bench guards play heavy roles at their current impact, Denver is a strong playoff team that is hard to trust in a series against the Bostons and Houstons. Murray's current level won't fully hold, so improvement has to come from the supporting cast rather than the stars.
swingFactors: Murray sustaining near his current efficiency
Defensive rebounding recovering toward last year's level

confidence.note: Eleven games and a soft recent schedule, but five seasons of history anchor the read.
